uncited: Selective and Budgeted Rendering accelerates volume rendering by leveraging hierarchical data structures to avoid redundant computation, either by reusing unchanged partial images over time or by skipping low-complexity regions based on error metrics.

It differs from standard hierarchical traversal by introducing temporal persistence (compositing trees) or statistical bounds (entropy) to control rendering budget, whereas siblings like [DDA Tree Traversal with Mini-Stack](5244-dda-tree-traversal-with-mini-stack.md) focus on spatial traversal efficiency without temporal or statistical pruning.
All methods utilize an octree structure where nodes represent spatial subdivisions.
Specific to this family, nodes may store auxiliary data (partial images or entropy metrics) that influence the traversal path or the final pixel value computation.
Selective and Budgeted Rendering originated in the context of time-varying volume data visualization, where inter-frame delay and storage space were significant bottlenecks.
The approach was developed to leverage hierarchical data structures for both compression and rendering acceleration.
The method is particularly relevant for scientific visualization of dynamic datasets where significant portions of the volume remain constant between time steps.
